The Story of the Fish and the Power of Thought

I bow to Lord Adinath, who holds the eye of omniscience and is self-manifest, and I write a story so that the noble may understand how much sin and karmic bondage arises from mere mental thought — from thinking alone in the mind.

In the self-manifest ocean at the farthest end, there lives a massive fish of enormous body. It is a thousand yojanas long, five hundred yojanas wide, and two hundred and fifty yojanas tall. (One yojana equals four or two thousand miles.) Near this great fish, around its ears, lives another fish named Shalisiktha. But this one is very small and feeds on the dirt from the great fish's ears.

When the great fish has eaten hundreds of small water creatures and lies with its mouth open, sunk in six months of deep, snoring sleep, then small creatures — turtles, fish, alligators, and crocodiles a yojana or two long — boldly enter and exit through its fearsome, fanged mouth. At that time, the small Siktha fish thinks every day: "How foolish this great fish is, letting creatures who come easily into its mouth go free for no reason. If only I had that power, I would never let a single creature escape."

It is deeply sad that sinful people, through such evil thoughts alone, bind great sins and fall into lower births, where they suffer many torments. This was the fate of the Siktha fish too. Through such evil thoughts, it bound intense karmas and went to the seventh hell. For it is the mind's thoughts that are the cause of merit or sin. Therefore, the noble should always keep the mind pure through the study and teaching of Jain scriptures, so that evil thoughts cannot enter. And without the study of scriptures, one cannot know good from bad. Therefore, scriptural study is the primary cause of purity.

This word of Jina is the lamp that destroys the darkness of false faith. It uproots the sufferings of the world from their very root. It is the cause of the happiness of liberation itself, and is worthy of the respect of all great beings — gods, Vidyadharas, and others. All worship this word of Jina with great devotion. You too should always practise, reflect upon, and contemplate this sacred word of Jina for peace and happiness.

This story teaches that even thoughts alone — without any physical action — can create karmic bondage. The small fish never actually harmed anyone, yet its evil thoughts of wanting to trap creatures led it to hell. The wise should guard their minds as carefully as they guard their actions, for the mind is the source of all karma.
